subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps (streaming, function calling, embeddings/reranking)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chan <alex@fabrikatech.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps (streaming, function calling, embeddings/reranking)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call to make sure we captured the right pain points and next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- UI latency on product search and detail pages (95th pct > 800ms for search suggestions).
- Cost unpredictability when scaling embeddings/reranking across catalogs (daily spikes during promotions).
- Difficulty returning structured product metadata from the model reliably (need consistent fields for downstream indexing).
- Need to call internal pricing and inventory APIs from the model (function calling / tool integration).

Goals you shared:
- Reduce tail latency for search & typeahead to <200ms for 95th pct.
- Move embeddings + reranking to a predictable cost model and reduce per-query spend by at least 30%.
- Get deterministic structured outputs for product attributes (sku, price, availability).
- Prototype streaming results in the UI for progressive render of suggestions.

What we propose (high-level):
- SDK integration: Python + Node reference SDKs and a short integration guide — small changes to how you call streaming + function-calling endpoints.
- Function calling: Redwood can call your internal pricing & inventory endpoints via a secure, signed webhook pattern or you can implement a small adapter inside your VPC/private deployment.
- Streaming & structured outputs: stream tokens for UI responsiveness and provide JSON schema enforcement and structured output post-processing to ensure consistent fields.
- Embeddings & reranking: recommend a hybrid approach (dense + sparse) and a rerank model that runs on dedicated instances to stabilize cost; include prefix caching for frequent SKUs.

Next steps / actions (owners & ETA):
- Deliver proposal + integration guide (Marissa) — ETA: Wed, 2026-03-04.
- Share sample SDK snippet for streaming + function-calling (Marissa).
- Fabrikatech to share a short list of 3 example queries + expected structured outputs (Alex) — ETA: Tue, 2026-03-03.
- Technical sync (30–45m) with engineering to walk the SDK and auth options (Vivek/Rishi to join) — target week of 2026-03-09.

Attachments I will send: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf, sdk-integration-guide.md, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

If that looks right I will follow up with the proposal and the SDK guide tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0123

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps (streaming, function calling, embeddings/reranking)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the tidy recap — that matches what we discussed. A few clarifications/questions from our side:

1) For function calling: we prefer the model to call a thin internal adapter that sits behind our auth layer (no direct outbound webhooks). Can you outline the adapter contract (auth, payload shape) in the SDK guide?

2) Streaming: important that partial results are meaningful — are you able to show an example of a progressive suggestion UX with token-level streaming?

3) Embeddings: curious about your recommended dimensionality and whether you support on-the-fly reindexing without downtime. We have ~2M SKUs and need minimal disruption.

We will compile 3 example queries and expected JSON outputs (Priya will own) and aim to have that to you by EOB Tue 3/3 PST.

Also, can you include an expected cost estimate for our typical peak qps (~120 qps) in the proposal?

Cheers,
Alex
Head of Product Engineering
Fabrikatech
alex@fabrikatech.com

Alex/Priya —

Appreciate the quick responses and the ask list. Attached are the items I promised:
- redwood-integration-proposal.pdf (overview, cost estimate for 120 qps peak, recommended deployment mode: Dedicated with burst pool)
- sdk-integration-guide.md (Python & Node examples for streaming + function calling; adapter contract appendix)
- mutual-action-plan.xlsx (milestones and owners)

Key points from the attachments:
- Adapter contract: signed JWT auth + short-lived bearer token, payload is JSON with {query, context, session_id}; response should be JSON with {content, metadata, tool_calls} — full schema in the SDK guide.
- Streaming snippet: we included both a token-stream example and a chunked JSON mode for progressive UI rendering (see examples on page 3 of sdk-integration-guide.md).
- Structured outputs: we recommend using Redwood's schema enforcement layer (schema-first outputs + soft-validation) to ensure fields like sku, price, availability are always produced.
- Embeddings: recommend 768 dims (for hybrid dense+sparse) and a rolling reindex approach using blue/green indices to avoid downtime. Cost estimate attached uses a mix of Dedicated inference for rerank and Hosted for occasional burst.

Next steps (updated):
- Fabrikatech to send example queries + expected JSON (Priya) — ETA: Wed, 2026-03-04 EOD.
- Schedule technical sync: propose Thu, 2026-03-12 14:00 PST / 17:00 EST (30–45m). Vivek/Rishi will join. Please confirm availability.
- We will share a short proof-of-concept plan (2-week pilot) after the sync with a small dataset and success criteria.

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf, sdk-integration-guide.md, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks — sending to HubSpot as well and will follow up with calendar invites once you confirm the sync.

Best,
